WESTERN
W
HOTELS
PUNGE
NEW WASHNGTON HOTEL
SEATTLE
Jan. 26,1933.
Dear Debby;
This letter to you is for me what Hoboken is for the
Theatrical producers - I am trying out my skill on the Corona.
Looks pretty good so far n° est pas!
I was very lucky it seems to get through to Portland
by air,as no ships came over the route from Salt Lake either be-
fore or since within a twenty four hour period. The weather was
perfect when we came except for a few snow storms.The trip down
the Columbia River Canyon was beautiful or rather it was grand.
Great snow covered mountains towering above us on either side
with the water down below boiling and churning over the rocks
and down the rapids. The sun was setting right in front of us
behind a mountain of clouds rising thousands of feet into the
sky. Later as we got down toward where the River broadens out
to a mile or more the sun had gone down and the light of Van-
couver, Washington showed on our left. Farther on to the right
other little town lights twinkled and then as we passed over
the river and headed slightly Southwest we could see the red
Neon sign of the Richfield Oil Co. It is on top o I a tall off-
ice building in Portland and each letter of RICHFIELD is sixty
feet high. Then the thousands of lights of the city, a swift
ride over the outskirts and we circled the Airport which is
located on an island in the bay or harbor. The flood lights of
the field came on and we glide d down to a perfect landing.
carry me on for another hour and a half flight to Seattle was
forced down by bad visibility in California - believe it or not-
and they advised me
at the Airport that if I wanted to get to
Seattle it would be well to take the train as the prediction for
today was very bad.
Arrived here thes morning and found Groeger , my
traveling companion, waiting for me. He ,by the way, wears very
well and see ms to know the technical side of airtransport from
A to Z.
As I told you before leaving I will typewrite some of
my letters to you making copies which I will send to Frances and
Bo and to the family. This is the first of that series and in
spite of the seek and peck system of typing I think the net re-
sult is a considerable saving of time. I hope none of those on
the receiving end will feel slighted. I really have a lot of letters
to write and a lot of paper work to do.
My love to you and Cat and Hebe,
